categories.main_business_segments: AES operates two primary business lines: generation (owning and operating power plants to generate and sell electricity) and utilities (owning and operating electricity distribution and transmission utilities). The company is organized into four geographic Strategic Business Units (SBUs): US and Utilities (United States, Puerto Rico, El Salvador), South America (Chile, Colombia, Argentina, Brazil), MCAC (Mexico, Central America, Caribbean), and Eurasia (Europe and Asia).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: AES leverages a diverse mix of technologies including renewable energy (solar, wind, hydro, energy storage), thermal generation (natural gas, coal, oil, pet coke), and advanced grid solutions. The company is a leader in battery energy storage (through Fluence), and is developing green hydrogen, digital energy platforms, and innovative hybrid solutions such as 'Green Blend' (integrating renewables with thermal generation). AES also utilizes advanced environmental controls and grid modernization technologies.
categories.primary_customers_markets: AES serves a wide range of customers including wholesale utilities, industrial and commercial users, government entities, and end-use residential customers through its utilities. Key end markets include large corporate buyers (notably technology and data center companies), regulated utility customers, and industrial sectors such as mining. No single customer accounts for more than 10% of total revenue.
categories.geographic_coverage: AES operates in 14 countries across the Americas, Europe, and Asia. Major regions include the United States, South America (notably Chile, Brazil, Colombia, Argentina), Central America and the Caribbean (Dominican Republic, Panama, Mexico, El Salvador), and Eurasia (Bulgaria, Vietnam, Jordan, India, Netherlands). The company’s assets are geographically diversified, with significant renewable and thermal portfolios in each region.
categories.supply_chain_position: AES primarily operates as an independent power producer (IPP) and utility, positioned downstream in the energy supply chain. It generates, transmits, and distributes electricity to wholesale and retail customers, and is increasingly involved in energy storage, grid services, and energy solutions for end-users. The company also participates in LNG import and regasification infrastructure in select markets.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: AES’s strategic focus is on accelerating the transition to clean energy, with priorities including expanding renewable generation, energy storage, and digital energy solutions. The company invests in R&D through its AES Next incubator, targeting innovations in green hydrogen, advanced storage, digital platforms, and grid modernization. AES emphasizes customer co-creation, decarbonization, and the development of new business models to support net-zero goals.
categories.revenue_model: AES generates revenue primarily through long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs), regulated utility tariffs, and spot market electricity sales. Additional revenue streams include capacity payments, ancillary grid services, energy storage solutions, and, in some markets, LNG sales and infrastructure services. The company also benefits from renewable energy tax credits and, through equity interests, from technology licensing and digital services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: AES competes with global and regional independent power producers, utilities, and renewable energy developers such as NextEra, Enel, Engie, Iberdrola, and local incumbents in each market. It is positioned as a leading global clean energy developer, recognized for its scale in corporate renewables, innovation in storage (via Fluence), and its ability to deliver integrated, customer-centric energy solutions.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2022, AES reported $12.6 billion in revenue, with approximately 32,000 MW of generation capacity and 2.6 million utility customers. The company is experiencing strong growth in renewables, with a 64 GW development pipeline and a 12.2 GW contracted backlog. While recent years included significant asset impairments and net losses, adjusted EPS and operating cash flow remain robust, and capital expenditures are focused on renewables and grid modernization.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: AES differentiates itself through its ability to deliver tailored, innovative clean energy solutions at scale, including 24/7 carbon-free energy for large corporates, integrated renewables and storage, and advanced digital platforms. Its global footprint, strong customer partnerships, and leadership in energy storage and decarbonization position it as a trusted partner for customers seeking to achieve ambitious sustainability and reliability goals.
